questions.question: How can you simulate orbital paths of planets revolving around the Sun in our 3D Solar System?
options: Using the 'orbit around' block connecting target coordinate X, Y, Z
questions.explanation: Correct! The 'orbit around' block sweeps a sprite in circular paths around a focal coordinate.

questions.question: Which celestial body is at the absolute center of our Solar System model?
questions.explanation: Excellent! The Sun is the gravity center around which all planets orbit.

questions.question: Which planetary motion is created when a planet revolves around its own internal center (creating day/night)?
questions.explanation: Perfect! Rotation (spinning) causes planets to spin on their own axis.

questions.question: If Earth takes 365 days to orbit the Sun and Mercury takes 88 days, how should we code their orbital speeds?
options: Earth should be faster than Mercury
Mercury orbital speed should be set faster than Earth's orbital speed
Both should have the same speed
questions.explanation: Spot on! Mercury orbits closer and much faster, so we give it a higher orbital speed value.

questions.question: What type of light source radiates light beams equally in all directions (like a lightbulb or our Sun)?
questions.explanation: Great! A Point Light acts like an incandescent bulb, illuminating surrounding objects 360-degrees around.

questions.question: Which block is used to set the color of an added virtual light source?
questions.explanation: Perfect! 'set light color' changes the glow color (e.g. Red for hot warning, Yellow for cozy suns).

questions.question: What property of a virtual light source controls how bright the light shines?
questions.explanation: Spot on! Intensity determines light output brightness; high intensity creates glaring glows.

questions.question: How do you make a planet look realistic (e.g. displaying oceans and continents on Earth)?
options: Apply a planet sphere texture mapping
questions.explanation: Great! Applying 3D texture maps wraps a planet graphic onto the sphere sprite body.

questions.question: Why did we place colored point lights in front of our alphabet letters project?
options: To make them look like glowing neon signs in a 3D night scene!
questions.explanation: Excellent! Point lights cast glowing rays on letter panels, mimicking neon glow arts.

questions.question: What coordinate should match for a Moon orbiting around the Earth?
options: The Moon's orbit center must get Earth's X, Y, Z coordinates
questions.explanation: Perfect! The Moon's orbital center must track the moving Earth, so it sweeps around the planet.

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to make a planet sprite orbit around coordinates (0, 0, 0) at a speed of 5 degrees per tick.
questions.task_hint: orbit around X(0) Y(0) Z(0) speed(5)
questions.explanation: Outstanding! Snapping this block creates a beautiful, revolving planetary system!

questions.question: Coding Task: Write block pseudo-code to place a Point Light at coordinates X=0, Y=50, Z=100 with a bright Yellow color.
questions.task_hint: add point light at X(0) Y(50) Z(100) -> set light color to Yellow
questions.explanation: Perfect! This positions a radiant sun glow directly in the center of the 3D scene!
